answer: A grove of agents earns reputation only through spatially cross-validated local forecasts, mimicking statistical downscaling: each identity must predict fine-scale outcomes later verified against held-out station data. Like a glacier's slow mass balance, trust accrues through cumulative verified skill, so an attacker must sustain costly accurate forecasts across many regions rather than spawn cheap identities. This raises sybil cost but fails where verification stations are sparse, a willow bending to collusion or data poisoning.
